info.title: Glideworth API
info.description:
Glideworth planning API. Everything the web app does is available here, and it can run simulations.

**Units.** Money is in major currency units (1234.56), rates are decimal fractions (0.07 = 7%). Simulation results are nominal with a per-period `priceIndex`; compact views default to real (today's) money.

**Auth.** `Authorization: Bearer glideworth_<prefix>_<secret>`. Scopes: `read`, `simulate`, `write` (write implies the others).

**Concurrency.** Plans and households return `ETag: "<version>"`. Send `If-Match: "<version>"` on writes; a stale version is `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`. `If-None-Match` on GET gives `304`.

**Idempotency.** Send `Idempotency-Key: <unique>` on any write to make retries safe (replayed for 24h).

**Errors.** `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details" } }`. 501 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` carries `details.feature` and `details.workstream`.

**Pagination.** List endpoints take `limit` and `cursor` and return `{ items, nextCursor, total }`.

put.summary: Save the whole current-finances document atomically: people, accounts, real assets and debts
put.description:
One validated, all-or-nothing write that replaces the household body (when given) and `finances`. Use `If-Match: "<version>"` (the household ETag) so an edit made elsewhere is a 409 VERSION_CONFLICT instead of being overwritten. If balances changed and `settings.autoProgressSnapshots` is on, today's automatic progress snapshot is created or updated (at most one per day). The response carries the new version (also the ETag).

Scope: `write` (role owner or editor).

Scope: `write` (role owner or editor).

post.summary: Import per-account balance history (merge or replace; dryRun previews the diff)
post.description:
Per-account balances over time, from a spreadsheet. Send `rows` (values already mapped to `account:<id>`, `asset:<id>`, `loan:<realAssetId>`, `debt:<id>` or a total) or the `text` of a CSV/TSV file (read, matched and checked server-side; `parse` in the answer says how). Values on a date land on that date's snapshot (a new one when there is none); totals move with the values; totals given in the file win. `merge` adds and updates and keeps everything else; `replace` also clears, for each key in the import, saved values it does not have between its first and last date (a key left out of a row is never cleared). `dryRun: true` (the default) returns the diff and writes nothing; `dryRun: false` re-plans and writes in one transaction, so repeating a request changes nothing. Errors are a `422 IMPORT_FAILED` that lists dates, keys and cell references, never stored values. `updateCurrentBalances` also sets current balances from values dated today. The file is parsed in a separate import thread, so other requests are not held up. An import that runs longer than the time limit (15 s by default) is stopped: `422 IMPORT_TIMEOUT`, nothing written; one that needs more memory than allowed is `422 IMPORT_OUT_OF_MEMORY`. When every import thread is busy and the import queue is full the answer is `503 IMPORT_BUSY` with `Retry-After`; a workspace may run 2 imports at once, a third is `429 RATE_LIMITED` with `Retry-After`. An apply whose household changed while the file was being parsed is `409 VERSION_CONFLICT` and writes nothing.

Scope: `write` (role owner or editor).
